clues: A gorge in west Bolivia holds this city. It sits southeast of big Lake Titicaca.
Because the city sits so high, its climate is odd for the tropics. Summers bring rain, but winters stay dry.
A Spanish captain founded it on 20 October 1548. He built it where an Inca town had stood.
Here is a fun one to retell. This city has the world's largest city cable car network.
Snow tops Illimani, a peak with three tops, all year. You can see it from much of this city.
